title: Static, Sliding & Rolling
description: The final shards need a moving cart. Discover why rolling beats sliding — the key to defeating Baron Standstill.

content.value: Friction comes in different strengths depending on how surfaces move over each other. The three main types are static, sliding and rolling friction.

STATIC friction  → acts when an object is about to move (strongest)
SLIDING friction → acts when an object slides over a surface
ROLLING friction → acts when an object rolls (weakest)

Strength:   STATIC  >  SLIDING  >  ROLLING

STATIC friction acts on an object that is at rest but about to move. It's why a heavy box is hardest to get moving at the very start. Once it starts sliding, less force is needed to keep it going — because sliding friction is smaller than static friction.

ROLLING friction is much smaller than sliding friction. That's the genius of the WHEEL — rolling a load is far easier than dragging it. This is also why machines use ball bearings: tiny balls let parts roll instead of slide, cutting friction dramatically.
Remember the order from strongest to weakest: STATIC > SLIDING > ROLLING. Turning sliding into rolling (with wheels or bearings) is one of humanity's greatest inventions.
Key Takeaway: Static friction (about to move) is strongest, sliding friction is smaller, and rolling friction is weakest. Wheels and ball bearings replace sliding with rolling to reduce friction.

quiz.question: Which type of friction is the WEAKEST?
quiz.explain: Rolling friction is the smallest, which is why rolling a load is easier than dragging it.
